worlds.label: ARQ house loop volume
worlds.description: Localized temporal battery; memory bleed escalates

events.label: Renton wakes with Hannah; Bloc raid begins
events.description: Renton wakes beside his girlfriend Hannah in a house where time has just started over - and armed raiders burst in, beginning a morning he will live many times.

events.label: Renton dies escaping; first reset
events.description: Trying to flee the raiders, Renton is shot dead - and immediately wakes back in bed at the start of the same morning.

events.label: ARQ resets interval; Renton retains memory
events.description: The house's mysterious machine, the ARQ, has restarted the day, but Renton alone carries his memories forward into the repeat.

events.label: Hannah revealed as Bloc Mother; trust fractures
events.description: Hannah turns out to be an agent of the Bloc, the group after the ARQ - and Renton learns the woman beside him has been lying about who she is.

events.label: Renton theorizes ARQ loops house volume as temporal battery
events.description: Renton works out what the ARQ is: a machine that traps the whole house in a repeating stretch of time, its endless restarts storing energy like a battery.

events.label: Hannah retains memory across reset
events.description: After another reset Hannah starts remembering too - the two of them are now the only ones who know the day is repeating.

events.label: Sonny exposed as Torus mole
events.description: Sonny, the raiders' leader, is exposed as a spy for Torus, the corporation that will one day own the ARQ's technology.

events.label: Sonny retains memory; arms-race loops
events.description: Sonny gains the same memory-carrying advantage, and the loops turn into an arms race - each reset lets the different sides scheme further.

events.label: Aware Sonny saves Cuz from ARQ electrocution
events.description: With his new foreknowledge, Sonny saves his man Cuz from the ARQ's electric trap - small proof of how much the repeats can be exploited.

events.label: Escape proves loop is house-bounded
events.description: An escape attempt proves the loop's edges: the day resets only for the house and everything inside it - step outside and you keep whatever you find.

events.label: Logs reveal outer nine-cycle wipe nesting inner loops
events.description: Hidden logs reveal worse news: this day-loop sits inside a larger cycle, nine repetitions wiped clean by something outside they cannot see.

events.label: Record message for future iterations; hope to deliver ARQ to Bloc
events.description: Renton and Hannah record a message for their future selves, hoping to finally hand the ARQ over to the Bloc and break the pattern.

events.label: Torus robot kills them; Hannah gasps awake
events.description: A Torus robot cuts the plan short, killing them both - and Hannah's sharp gasp as she wakes suggests the loop has not finished with them.

events.label: Implied outer/nested cycle continues
events.description: The implication hangs unspoken: the whole house-loop may itself be starting over from a point no one inside can remember.

events.label: Rentos wakes again in hijacked van
events.description: In the wider story, Renton wakes once more in the hijacked van where his loops began.

events.label: Wife/hostage dynamics across iterations
events.description: The hostages and captors shift roles across the repeats, each iteration rewriting who holds power in the van.

events.label: Corporate Renton antagonism
events.description: A harder Renton - the corporate variant - stands across from the man we know as the story's antagonist in the repeats.

events.label: Attempted escapes rewrite
events.description: Escape attempts pile up, each one rewriting the morning differently.

events.label: Final choice about looping tech
events.description: It ends on a choice about the looping technology itself - whether to use it, destroy it, or hand it on.

events.label: Blocking tech causes death-loop
events.description: The rule that binds them: blocking the machine's cycle kills - the loop keeps its prisoners by death as much as by walls.

events.label: Gas/ventilation tactics
events.description: Gas and ventilation become weapons across the iterations - controlling the air means controlling who wakes.

events.label: Ambiguous exit
events.description: The film closes on an ambiguous exit - out of the loop, perhaps, but into what is never shown.

ruleEffects.effect: Device loops a bounded volume until energy/strategy exit
Death returns to bedroom checkpoint with growing memory cohort

interventions.notes: Nested nine-cycle wipe adds outer checkpoint

ruleEffects.effect: Informational artifact aims to change future iterations' strategy

outcome.summary: No clean exit on screen; nested loops and Torus robot cliffhanger leave hope as a message to future iterations.
